sentences.text: Protoavis is reconstructed as a carnivorous animal with forward-facing eyes, suggesting a nocturnal or crepuscular lifestyle.
Reconstructions typically show Protoavis with feathers, based on the interpretation of arm structures as quill knobs.
It is usually depicted as a bipedal archosaur similar to poposaurids and rauisuchids of the same time period.
The braincase resembles that of Troodon, featuring an enlarged cerebellum that shifted optic lobes ventrolaterally and a large floccular lobe.
However, the specimen is notably non-bird-like in possessing only a single exit for the trigeminal nerve.
Protoavis fossils were discovered at the Tecovas and Bull Canyon Formations in the Texas panhandle in 1973.
These remains were found in Late Triassic Norian stage deposits near Post, Texas.
The fossils were found in a jumbled cache of disarticulated bones in Triassic river delta strata, possibly resulting from a mass mortality event caused by a flash flood.
Sankar Chatterjee originally interpreted the type specimen of Protoavis texensis as coming from a single animal.
Protoavis is classified within the superorder Dinosauria and order Saurischia.
It is further classified within the parent group Theropoda.
The animal is classified in the class Reptilia.
Protoavis lived during the Late Triassic period, approximately 210 million years ago in what is now North America.
The Dockum Group, where Protoavis fossils were found, dates from the Carnian to the early Norian stages of the terminal Triassic.
The paleoclimate of the Dockum Group was subtropical with a distinct dry and wet season pattern marked by monsoonal rains.
Botanical evidence indicates that the area where Protoavis lived was densely forested.
If Protoavis is correctly identified as a bird, its existence would push back the origins of avian life by 60 to 75 million years.
Many paleontologists doubt that Protoavis is a bird or that all assigned remains belong to a single species.
Some researchers suggest that portions of Protoavis may be of drepanosaurid nature.
The quadrates of specimens TTU P 9200 and TTU P 9201 are dissimilar, a fact difficult to explain if the material is conspecific, despite Chatterjee's insistence.
Subsequent re-evaluations, such as those by Lawrence Witmer, have been inconclusive about whether the arm structures are actual quill knobs.
